_about: Where each channel draws its own buttons and text over a vertical video, on the 1080x1920 canvas. Nothing that must be read (a word, a headline, a number, a logo, the point of a graphic) may sit in a zone of any channel the cut is filed for (scripts/channel_safe.py). Krish, 2026-11-03, on Monday's Instagram post: "It looks cramped. It looks like you almost didn't design this thoughtfully for the format or the channel." This table is never looser than config/studio.json's platform safe_zones (tests/channel_safe_test.py); studio.json carries these Instagram numbers since 3 Nov 2026 (Krish: "I approve updating the Instagram button zones"). Shapes: 'tall' for every frame of a tall cut; 'cover_tall' for the cover or thumbnail a tall cut posts with, which also must survive Instagram's 3:4 profile grid crop (post-mortem of 2 Nov, cause D).

instagram_reels.measured: 2026-11-03, from Krish's phone screenshot of Monday 2 Nov's Reel (923x2000 screen, video 1080x1920 at 0.855 scale from y 72): back arrow and camera to y 126; action rail x 895 to 1080, y 548 to 1671; avatar, handle, caption and 'Liked by' from y 1373; the comment bar hides everything below y 1747.

instagram_profile.measured: Not yet measured on his phone. 270 px is the top 14% that size guides give for Instagram's Reels overlay (reap.video; Instagram documents no number). Krish's 7 Nov screenshot (Bugs & Issues) shows the 6 Nov reel's title, whose first line the stage headline draws from y 220, under Instagram's account row when the reel is opened from the profile. Measure it on his phone and replace this line.

zones.name: account row (reel opened from the profile)

instagram_grid.measured: Geometry, not a guess: since January 2025 the profile grid shows a 9:16 reel's cover as a 3:4 tile, the middle 1080x1440 of the 1080x1920 frame, cutting 240 px at the top and the bottom (size guides; Instagram's Edit cover > Profile grid preview shows it). Krish, 7 Nov: the 6 Nov reel's cover lost its top line "USING A" on the grid ("the thumbnails need to be managed better"). A word that crosses the line is cut, so any overlap counts.
